claim: Let's Talk FPL reports Cherki was subbed at half-time against Man Utd in GW4 (game state, City down to 10 men) and Foden was sent off in the first half.
quote: Churkey was brought off at halftime against Man United in gameweek four and Foden was sent off in the first half.

claim: Let's Talk FPL says Foden's red card brings a three-match ban, but one is a Carabao Cup tie, so he misses Sunderland (H) in GW5 and Liverpool (A) in GW6 and returns for GW7.
quote: he's now suspended for three matches, but one of those matches is Carabal Cup. So he'll actually be back for gameweek seven.

claim: Let's Talk FPL says Foden is a straight sell rather than a two-week hold, since he isn't good enough to bench, his price will likely drop while out, and his minutes on return for GW7 aren't guaranteed.
quote: Fodden is just a sell for me very simply. He's not that good that I would bench him for two weeks.

claim: Let's Talk FPL finds it encouraging that Cherki started GW4 alongside Foden with Enzo and Anderson in midfield, and expects Cherki to start as the number 10 against Sunderland in GW5 with Foden suspended.
quote: the fact that Churkey and Foden started, I think that's quite good for Churkey... Churkeyy's gonna start number 10, I think, against Sunderland.

claim: Let's Talk FPL recommends holding Cherki for one more week (Sunderland at home) and deciding after the international break, rather than selling him to Gibbs-White now, since his price is depressed after two poor returns.
quote: I think you keep him for one week and you decide what to do after the international break.

claim: Let's Talk FPL reports O'Reilly was benched for GW4 vs Man Utd and only brought on in the second half, with Enzo playing midfield and Gvardiol playing the whole match at left-back.
quote: He was benched in gameweek four against Man United. He was brought on in the second half... Vardial played the whole game at left back.

claim: Let's Talk FPL notes O'Reilly hasn't started a game at left-back since the Community Shield, while Gvardiol has started all four league games there.
quote: Nikico O'Reilly hasn't started a game as a left back since the Community Shield... he has started the first four games at left back.

claim: Let's Talk FPL recommends selling O'Reilly despite the Sunderland home fixture, seeing no clear route to regular starts with Gvardiol at left-back and Anderson/Enzo dominant in midfield.
quote: I think he's probably got a go. I can't see a good reason to keep him.

claim: Let's Talk FPL thinks Enzo Fernandez could end up the Man City attacker (outside Haaland) getting the most minutes this season, with Elliot Anderson also nailed, squeezing out O'Reilly.
quote: Enzo Fernandez might end up being the Man City attacker outside of Harland that gets the most minutes this season.

claim: Let's Talk FPL lists Anderson, an unresolved player referred to as 'Batti', and O'Reilly as options who can all play Man City midfield, illustrating O'Reilly's competition for a starting spot.
quote: Anderson, Batti, O'Reilly, they can all play in midfield.

claim: Let's Talk FPL thinks Guéhi looks fairly nailed at left centre-back in the Man City defence and rates him an excellent option there.
quote: I think right now Gay looks fairly nailed in that defense. I think he's an excellent left center back.

claim: Let's Talk FPL raises uncertainty over the Man City back line if O'Reilly ever displaces Gvardiol at left-back: whether Guéhi shifts to right centre-back or Rúben (Dias) loses his place.
quote: What happens to Gay? Does he come out of the team? Does he go right center back? does Diaz come out of the team?

claim: Let's Talk FPL notes Szoboszlai has no open-play FPL attacking return this season: a GW1 penalty, GW2 defensive contribution, and blanks in GW3 and GW4.
quote: gameweek one the penalty, gameweek two, defcon, game weeks three and four were a blank.

claim: Let's Talk FPL cites Szoboszlai's GW4 expected goal involvement at 0.4, calling it pretty good for a nailed player and probable first-choice penalty taker.
quote: Sosai gets 0.4 expected goal involvement in gameweek four, which is pretty good to be honest.

claim: Let's Talk FPL says selling Szoboszlai is reasonable for anyone unhappy with him, but he personally is unlikely to sell this week, preferring to keep three free transfers banked for the international break.
quote: If you're not happy with Sosite, just sell him... I'm probably not going to sell him, but international break is a big part of that.

claim: Let's Talk FPL describes Szoboszlai's current number 8 role as only occasionally getting into the box, not enough to give the box-to-box excitement a front-three player offers.
quote: He's playing this number eight role where he does get forward at times... it's not happening all the time.

claim: Let's Talk FPL cites Schade's GW4 expected goal involvement at 0.31, slightly below Szoboszlai's, but notes Schade actually walked away with two goals that week.
quote: If you look at Sharda, he got 0.31... only Sharda walks away with two goals.

claim: Let's Talk FPL cites Groß's GW4 expected goal involvement at 1.01 (about 0.2 excluding the penalty) plus two assists, as a comparison point favouring cheaper alternatives over Szoboszlai.
quote: he gets uh 1.01 expected goal, but you take away the penalty, that's closer to 0.2, and he gets two assists.

claim: Let's Talk FPL recommends Gibbs-White at 7.9m as a strong buy: nailed, always plays 90, on penalties, and facing Coventry at home in what he calls one of the best fixtures on paper this season.
quote: I would be tempted just to go to Gibbs White at 7.9 million. Nailed on. Coventry at home, 90 minutes penalties.

claim: Let's Talk FPL cites Gibbs-White's underlying numbers this season as 0.18 expected goals per 90 and 0.28 expected assists per 90, though he expects the creativity to regress toward last season's level.
quote: 0.18 expected goals per 90, 0.28 expected assists.

claim: Let's Talk FPL flags Gibbs-White's fixtures turn tougher after this week: Palace away in GW6 is not bad, but Arsenal at home in GW7 is difficult before Sunderland away in GW8.
quote: Palace away in six is not bad either... Arsenal at home in seven is not great. And then I switch away in eight also looks not bad.

claim: Let's Talk FPL notes Rogers hasn't blanked yet this season: a goal against Fulham in GW1, an assist in GW2, a goal against Arsenal in GW3, and another goal in GW4.
quote: scored another goal in gameweek four after scoring against Arsenal in three, assist in gameweek two, and a goal in gameweek one against Fulham.

claim: Let's Talk FPL believes Chelsea's fixtures are good right up until gameweek 13, making Rogers worth considering despite the best entry point having already passed (before the Hull game).
quote: I think the fixtures for Chelsea are good right up until gameweek 13.

claim: Let's Talk FPL would buy Gibbs-White over Rogers this week for a 2m difference if choosing between the two, but would not personally move Rogers to Gibbs-White, preferring to save the transfer.
quote: for a 2 million difference, I would just buy Gibbs White this week... would I move Rogers to Gibbs White? Probably not.

claim: Let's Talk FPL reports the 5m Belloumi scored a brace against Chelsea while only 2.1% owned, but was subbed off in the 59th minute for reasons that didn't appear injury-related.
quote: Balumi from Hull who's a 5 million pound midfielder just scored a brace against Chelsea and he's only 2.1% owned... he got subbed off on the 59th minute.

claim: Let's Talk FPL cites Belloumi's underlying numbers of 0.13 expected goals per 90 and 0.04 expected assists per 90 as not screaming a run of attacking returns.
quote: 0.13 expected goals per 90, 0.04 expected assists, it doesn't scream, I'm about to get a ton of attacking returns.

claim: Let's Talk FPL advises against rushing to buy Belloumi as a differential and specifically against selling Gomez to fund him, even with Gomez facing Arsenal.
quote: if you've got Gomez at Brighton, there's no way I'd be using a transfer to sell him to a whole player.

claim: Let's Talk FPL reports Ben White appeared to pick up an injury and was subbed at half-time against Sunderland; the duration is unknown but there's a chance he misses GW5.
quote: Ben White looked to have picked up an injury and that's the reason he was subbed at Halime against Sunderland... I do think there's a chance that he will miss gameweek five.

claim: Let's Talk FPL would not rush to buy Timber even if White is out, citing Timber's own injury history and Brighton away being Arsenal's worst fixture until Liverpool in GW9.
quote: Personally, I probably wouldn't... it's Brighton away, which is Arsenal's worst fixture until Liverpool in gameweek nine.

claim: Let's Talk FPL notes Gyökeres played no minutes recently, which is good news for Saka as first-choice penalty taker whenever Gyökeres is off the pitch.
quote: no minutes for Yokarez. I think that's just really good for Saka. First choice penalty taken when he's not on the pitch.

claim: Let's Talk FPL notes Saka started three games this week (implying midweek involvement) as reassuring information for owners, with no need to panic.
quote: Saka started three games in a week. That's also pretty good information. So, if you've got Saka, no need to panic.

claim: Let's Talk FPL cites Man City's expected goals conceded across their first four games as 0.65, 0.66, 1.37 (vs Coventry) and 1.0, calling their defence decent - the next tier below Arsenal.
quote: The xG conceded in the first four games 0.65, 0.66, 1.37 against Coventry and then one in gameweek four.

claim: Let's Talk FPL notes Wirtz has only one return this season (one assist in the first four gameweeks) and, unlike Szoboszlai, isn't on penalties or guaranteed 90 minutes.
quote: Vert also only has one return this season like Seoslai. one assist in the first four game weeks... at least Seosai is on penalties and like almost guaranteed to play 90.

claim: Let's Talk FPL leans toward it being time to let Wirtz go, though he's fine with holding him one more week and deciding after the international break.
quote: yeah, I think it's probably just time to let Verts go... I don't hate holding him for gameweek five.

claim: Let's Talk FPL rates Tarkowski good for the next two gameweeks (Ipswich at home) but less sure after that once Everton's schedule toughens; as a defender he's safer to bench when needed.
quote: So I think Tarovs is good for two. After that, not so sure.

claim: Let's Talk FPL would avoid bringing in Everton assets before their Ipswich-home run ends, given tough fixtures after that: Chelsea at home, Arsenal away, Newcastle away.
quote: I wouldn't bring in a player before Chelsea at home Arsenal away, Newcastle away. I'd avoid them until after those fixtures.

claim: Let's Talk FPL likes the 5m Muharemović, with Palace at home in GW5 (bench him GW6 vs Arsenal), and playable in most weeks after, freeing money elsewhere.
quote: Maherovic has Palace at home game week five. You'd probably want to bench him game week six against Arsenal, but after that, he's playable in quite a few weeks and he's only 5 million.

claim: Let's Talk FPL notes Konsa has already recorded a defensive contribution point for Arsenal, and came close again against Sunderland after barely doing so at Villa.
quote: he's got Defcon once already for Arsenal which he barely did at Villa and he came very close against Sunderland as well.

claim: Let's Talk FPL calls Calafiori and Konsa good long-term Arsenal defender picks, and says he'll play triple Arsenal defence in GW6 (Leeds home), GW7 (Forest away) and GW8 (Everton home).

claim: Let's Talk FPL would not buy De Cuyper this week with Arsenal away, suggesting waiting until GW6 onward instead.
quote: I would not be buying the Kyper this week... it's Arsenal, right? So I don't think you need to buy him. Wait until gameweek six onwards.

claim: Let's Talk FPL says Sangaré is almost certainly starting, played 90 minutes in GW4, and looks nailed on for a defensive contribution against a weak Chelsea defence, with a chance of an attacking return too.
quote: Sangari is almost certainly going to start. He got 90 minutes in gameweek four... nailed on that he will get defcon against Chelsea. And also Chelsea defense is not very good.

claim: Let's Talk FPL is weighing a 4-3-3 with Konsa versus a 3-4-3 with Sangaré in his own line-up this week, currently favouring Sangaré.
quote: Do I play 4-33 with KZA or 343 with Sangari? Right now my favorite is Sangari.

claim: Let's Talk FPL leans toward Newcastle over Everton for value picks around Foden's price or below, preferring Barnes over Elanga for greater goal threat, pending seeing that evening's Newcastle game.

claim: Let's Talk FPL lists Barnes's fixture run as Hull home (GW5), Coventry away (GW6), Villa home, Palace away, Everton home, Fulham away - none he'd be worried to start him in.
quote: it's Hull at home in five, Coventry away in six then it's Villa at home, Palace away, Everton at home, Fulham away.

claim: Let's Talk FPL suggests benching Groß this week if already owned, or bringing him in from GW6 (Sunderland away, Palace home are decent, but Liverpool and City away follow in GW8/9).

claim: Let's Talk FPL would wait until GW8 to target Tavernier given Bournemouth face Liverpool then Chelsea, and flags added injury risk this week from Bournemouth's Thursday European fixture.

claim: Let's Talk FPL flags Man City (Carabao Cup) and Bournemouth (Thursday European match) as having midweek fixtures this week, adding rotation/injury risk to their assets.

claim: Let's Talk FPL floats that wildcard holders could patch in a Newcastle or Everton value pick this week and wildcard afterwards to fix the whole squad.

claim: Let's Talk FPL reports a lot of people are planning to wildcard in GW6.
quote: a lot of people are going to wild card in six.

claim: Let's Talk FPL has two free transfers and 1.1m in the bank, and plans to roll rather than transfer this week, preferring three free transfers after the three-week international break.

claim: Let's Talk FPL's GW5 team plays Raya (his only goalkeeper) and Calafiori as a double-up against Brighton away, without expecting a clean sheet - calling it Arsenal's worst gameweek for clean-sheet odds until GW9.

claim: Let's Talk FPL calls Lewis Hall a nice pick against Hull, describing him as the most attacking player in the Newcastle team.
quote: Lewis Hall, really nice pick against Hull. He's the most attacking player in that team.

claim: Let's Talk FPL expects Gvardiol to start left-back again against Sunderland, hoping O'Reilly gets the Carabao Cup start against Norwich instead so Gvardiol is rested for a fresher league start.

claim: Let's Talk FPL notes his triple Chelsea attack (Palmer, Rogers, João Pedro) doesn't need three-plus team goals to pay off - in GW4 Chelsea scored two and all three players returned.

claim: Let's Talk FPL notes he triple-captained Palmer previously and it wasn't great.
quote: I triple captain Palmer, it wasn't great.

claim: Let's Talk FPL is captaining Haaland in GW5.

claim: Let's Talk FPL's team was rated 87% by the Fantasy Football Hub app ahead of GW5, which he calls okay but not amazing.

claim: Let's Talk FPL mentions considering a transfer involving an unresolved player referred to as 'Sakarin' as one option alongside Szoboszlai to Gibbs-White.
